slides.title: Why the US, why now
K-beauty is where US facial skincare is growing: Korean brands delivered 39% of the category's growth since 2021

claims.claim: K-beauty is taking a growing share of a growing category
evidence: US facial skincare sales, $B, 2021–25: K-beauty brands 1.9; 2.3; 2.7; 3.1; 3.6
38.6% of the category's 2021–25 sales growth came from K-beauty brands

claims.claim: K-beauty brands: sales up 89% in four years, against 22% for the category, lifting their share from 9% to 15%
Other brands: up 15% over the same four years, so most of the category's momentum is Korean
For Onsoo: a fast-growing segment where buyers already accept Korean brands
The trade-press figure of a $5.2B US K-beauty market also counts makeup and hair care, so it is not used; this deck sizes facial skincare only

slides.title: Amazon is where US K-beauty sells, and social media, not the store shelf, is where buyers find new brands

claims.claim: Amazon is the largest K-beauty channel, ahead of specialty beauty retail
evidence: US K-beauty skincare sales by channel, 2025: Amazon 41%; Specialty beauty retail 27%; Mass retail 14%; Brand websites 12%; Other 6%
61% of K-beauty buyers buy it most often on Amazon, compared with 22% at specialty retail

claims.claim: TikTok beats stores more than two to one as the place buyers discover a brand
evidence: Where K-beauty buyers discovered their last new brand, Sep 2026: TikTok 38%; In a store 17%
Survey of 1,200 US women aged 18–44 who bought facial skincare in the last six months, September 2026

slides.title: The Amazon pilot shows real demand, with June units 89% above January, but repeat purchase still trails the benchmark

claims.claim: Monthly units rose every month of the pilot
evidence: Amazon pilot units sold per month, three SKUs, Jan–Jun 2026: 7,400; 8,600; 10,100; 11,800; 12,900; 14,000

claims.claim: Repeat is just below new US brands and far below Onsoo in Korea
evidence: 90-day repeat purchase rate: Onsoo, US pilot 29%; First-year skincare brands, Amazon US 31%; Onsoo, Korea 48%

claims.claim: Ratings average 4.5 stars from 2,140 reviews; the top complaint, Korean-only labels in 6% of reviews, is fixed by the US labels in setup
evidence: 4.5 stars
2,140 reviews
6% of reviews

slides.title: Why not a national retail launch
Even on the planning team's own inputs, the retail-led route breaks the $18M cash cap in 2029 and never pays back

claims.claim: Fixed retail costs, not the sales plan, sink Option B
evidence: Board cap -18
115.5% of the board's cash cap used by end-2030, and still falling
$8.5M 2030 contribution, Amazon and retail − $9.8M 2030 fixed costs and fixtures = −$1.3M 2030 operating loss, the best year

claims.claim: Fixed cost: national marketing and field sales add $7.5M a year; at $7.55 a unit, retail would need about 32 units per door a week to cover it
Margin floor: the 2027 US loss would cut group operating margin to 4.5%, below the 8% floor
Amazon-led: on the same inputs it stays shallow and is back above zero in 2030

slides.title: At Onsoo's awareness, a newcomer sells about 2.6 units per door a week, well short of the 4.0 the retailer requires

claims.claim: The plan assumes survivors' sell-through
evidence: Median units per door per week by aided awareness, 2025: Below 10% 2.6; 10–20% 3.5; Above 20% 4.6; Option B plan 4.5
Removal line 4.0
1.7x planned sell-through over the median at Onsoo's awareness
The plan's 4.5 units comes from the retailer's deck on successful newcomers, which leaves out brands that were removed

claims.claim: Below 10%: Onsoo has 4% aided awareness; this band's top quartile sells only 3.4
Above 20%: the only band whose median clears the line
Specialty retail waits until aided awareness passes 20%
evidence: Retail analytics firm, 46 newcomer brands, 2025; the leading specialty retailer removes newcomers below 4.0 units per door per week after 12 months

slides.title: Precedents favor Amazon first, though it is no guarantee: the one retail-first entrant was removed from shelves

claims.claim: A door launch before awareness: the path Option B would repeat
evidence: Mooncrest | Retail-first, 2023, 450 doors | Removed from shelves in 2025; estimated cumulative US loss of $21M

claims.claim: Doors followed Amazon scale; the memo's 0.71 correlation between doors and Amazon sales fits this order too, so it cannot prove Option B's 1.3 times halo
evidence: Saebom | Amazon-first, 2022 | About $30M US revenue in 2025; added 300 retail doors in 2025
Board memo: correlation of 0.71 between specialty-retail doors and Amazon sales across 30 K-beauty brands in the US; a correlation does not show which one drives the other

claims.claim: Amazon alone does not ensure scale, which is why the launch needs gates
evidence: Gaon Lab | Amazon-first, 2022 | Below $5M US revenue in 2025

claims.claim: Same lesson: watch ad cost and repeat before scaling
evidence: Yeoreum | Amazon-first, 2023 | Below $5M US revenue in 2025

slides.title: Why Amazon-led entry
Advertising, the one cost Onsoo controls, is the largest in each $24 Amazon sale and leaves about $4 of contribution

claims.claim: Ad cost is the swing line in the unit economics
evidence: $ per unit at 28% ad cost and 15% duty: Price 24; Referral fee 3.6; FBA fee 5.1; Product cost 3.5; Freight and duty 1.075; Advertising 6.72; Contribution 4.005
16.7% of the price left as contribution after ads

claims.claim: Advertising: at 28% of the price, more than the FBA fee and the one line Onsoo controls
Each point of ad cost: takes $0.24 off every unit
Contribution per unit at the 32% ad cost of scaling brands
Price is held at $24: 52% of US buyers who tried K-beauty cite its price compared with US brands as a reason

slides.title: Only Amazon-led entry can pass all three board tests and build a US business, and only near the pilot's ad cost

claims.claim: A · Amazon-led, 28% ad cost: Recommended, with an ad-cost ceiling; passes all three tests if ad cost is held near the pilot's rate
evidence: 2030 revenue $26.4M; peak cumulative cash −$2.4M; cumulative cash end-2030 $0.4M; lowest group margin 9.3%

claims.claim: A · Amazon-led, 32% ad cost: Misses payback by 2030, though far inside the cap and the floor
B · Retail-led: Fails all three tests, even on its own inputs
J · Japan scale-up: Passes, but adds only incremental Japan revenue and no US business
evidence: Japan: no working-capital input is given, so operating profit stands in for cash

slides.title: Japan earns more until 2029, when Amazon-led entry overtakes it; by 2030 the US earns 1.8 times as much

claims.claim: The US is the bigger prize; Japan is the safer fallback
evidence: Operating profit added, $M, 2027–30: A · Amazon-led -1.6985; 0.1428; 1.3043; 2.3055
J · Japan scale-up -1.05; 0.55; 1; 1.3
1.8x Amazon-led 2030 operating profit as a multiple of Japan's

claims.claim: 2027–28: the US carries its $0.8M setup and ramp-up
2027–30 total: $2.1M from the US against $1.8M from Japan; at 32% ad cost the US adds −$0.6M
How the 2030 US profit is built
evidence: $4.4M contribution: 1,100k Amazon units × $4.01 after ads − $2.1M compliance, US team and off-Amazon marketing a year = $2.3M US operating profit in 2030

claims.claim: Japan's ceiling: a market growing 1.5% a year, where Onsoo already holds 3.1%
Waiting a year: US revenue in 2030 would sit near $20.4M

slides.title: Amazon-led entry reaches $26M by 2030, not $40M; even at its 2030 growth rate, $40M takes two more years

claims.claim: Read the ambition as a path: no modeled route hits $40M in 2030
evidence: Board ambition $40.0M
Board ambition: a US business "on the way to $40M revenue by 2030"

claims.claim: 2030: the plan's 1,100k units at $24 reach about two-thirds of the ambition
Retail-led plan: even its $37.6M in 2030 misses $40M, at a cash cost above the cap
$40M in 2030: would need 1,667k Amazon units at $24, 52% more than the plan
How we projected 2031–32
evidence: $26.4M × 1.3x × 1.3x = $44.2M projected 2032 revenue, Amazon only

claims.claim: Slowing growth: unit growth falls from 87% in 2028 to 52% and then 29%; if it keeps slowing, $40M comes after 2032

slides.title: What could break it, and how to launch
Payback by 2030 holds only while Amazon ad cost stays below about 29% of sales

claims.claim: Ad cost decides payback; the downside stays bounded
evidence: Option A cumulative US cash end-2030, $M: Planning 25% 2.3997; Pilot rate 28% 0.3766; 28% and 25% duty -0.7352; Scale benchmark 32% -2.3211; Stress 32% and 25% duty -3.4328

claims.claim: 32%: the median for brands growing from $5M to $20M a year, as Onsoo would in 2027–29
evidence: 32% is the agency median ad cost for skincare brands scaling from $5M to $20M a year (range 26%–38%)

claims.claim: Tariff: a 25% duty alone turns the 28% case negative
Stress: outflow peaks at $3.9M, 22% of the cap
Break-even ad cost for payback by end-2030
evidence: $19.3M cash left for ads ÷ $67.4M Amazon sales

claims.claim: How the 28% case is built
evidence: $11.3M contribution after ads: 2,810k units × $4.01 − $9.2M fixed costs and setup, 2027–30 − $1.7M inventory held at end-2030 = $0.4M cumulative cash, end-2030

slides.title: The 29% line leaves little room: the pilot already runs at 28%, and brands at Onsoo's planned scale pay 32%

claims.claim: Break-even ad cost for payback by end-2030
evidence: $19.3M cash left for advertising over 2027–30 if cumulative cash ends at zero ÷ $67.4M Amazon sales over 2027–30: 2,810k units at $24 = 28.6%

claims.claim: The line rests on the planning team's volumes and today's duty
evidence: Contribution before ads of $10.73 a unit × 2,810k units gives $30.1M over the four years
Fixed and one-time costs of $9.2M and $1.68M of year-end inventory come off first
Volumes follow the plan, from 300k units in 2027 to 1,100k in 2030; 4% fewer units miss payback at 28%
Duty stays at 15%; at 25% the line falls to 26.9%, below the pilot's rate
No Amazon returns cost is in the planning inputs; a 4% allowance like retail's would lower the line to 24.6%

claims.claim: Scaling brands pay 3.4 percentage points above the line: ad cost must be held as SKUs and volume grow

slides.title: Five gates keep the launch inside the board's limits and decide when retail is added

claims.claim: Gate 1 · Amazon ad cost, trailing quarter
evidence: Above 28.6% of sales (26.9% if duty rises) | Quarterly from Q3 2027 | Cap bids to hold the ceiling even if volume slows; above 32% for two quarters, cut back and move the 2028 slot to Japan

claims.claim: Gate 2 · US duty on Korean cosmetics
evidence: Rises from 15% to 25% | Mid-2027 decision | Tighten gate 1 to 26.9% and re-run the plan

claims.claim: Gate 3 · Amazon units against plan
evidence: Below 96% of plan (288k units in 2027) | End-2027 review | Hold the 2028 spend step-up until volume recovers

claims.claim: Gate 4 · 90-day repeat purchase
evidence: Below the 31% first-year benchmark | End-2027 review | Fix labels and listings before adding SKUs

claims.claim: Gate 5 · Retail entry trigger
evidence: Aided awareness above 20% and Amazon sales above $10M | Yearly survey from 2028 | Raise the CEO's 15% trigger to 20%
At 10–20% awareness the median newcomer sells 3.5 units per door a week, below the 4.0 removal line; 20% is needed, not sufficient

slides.title: The launch runs on Amazon from mid-2027, with a gate review at year-end and retail no earlier than 2029

claims.claim: Launch plan by workstream
evidence: Board decision, Tariff decision, Gate review milestones across Q1 2027–2030
Setup: US entity, MoCRA registration, US labels
Amazon: Own listings; add four SKUs; Scale if gates hold
Brand building: Social and influencer marketing; yearly awareness survey
Specialty retail: Test doors only if gate 5 is met
Japan: Fallback slot

claims.claim: The end-2027 review is the real go or no-go: ad cost, volume, repeat and the tariff are known by then, and stopping costs about $2.2M–2.4M
The Japan slot is used only if gates 1 or 3 fail, since management can run one major launch at a time

slides.title: Next steps

normalized.recommendation: Approve Amazon-led US entry with a 28.6% ad-cost ceiling and five gates, accepting up to $3.9M of outflow if payback slips (Enter the US in 2027 through Amazon, not 600 retail doors, and cap ad cost below about 29% of sales; retail waits for 20% awareness; if gates fail at end-2027, switch to Japan in 2028)

alternatives_considered.treatment: Recommended, with an ad-cost ceiling; passes all three tests if ad cost is held near the pilot's rate. At 32% ad cost it misses payback by 2030, though far inside the cap and the floor.

Rejected: fails all three tests, even on its own inputs; cumulative outflow reaches $20.8M by 2030, above the $18M cap; group margin 4.5% in 2027 below 8% floor; at Onsoo's awareness newcomers sell 2.6 units per door a week, short of the 4.0 removal line.
Passes, but adds only incremental Japan revenue and no US business; by 2030 the US earns 1.8 times as much. Kept as the safer fallback: switch to Japan in 2028 if gates 1 or 3 fail.

alternatives_considered.option: Waiting a year to enter the US
alternatives_considered.treatment: US revenue in 2030 would sit near $20.4M.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Synthetic benchmark data; every number from the briefing pack
Team model from the briefing pack: hero-product unit economics on every SKU, four months of landed cost held as inventory
The break-even line rests on the planning team's volumes and today's duty; 4% fewer units miss payback at 28%
Duty stays at 15%; at 25% the break-even line falls to 26.9%, below the pilot's rate; a 25% duty alone turns the 28% case negative
No Amazon returns cost is in the planning inputs; a 4% allowance like retail's would lower the line to 24.6%
Brands at Onsoo's planned scale pay 32% ad cost (agency median, range 26%–38%); at 32% cash is −$2.3M at end-2030
Japan: no working-capital input is given, so operating profit stands in for cash
Holding the 2030 growth rate is optimistic, since growth slows every year of the plan; the projection shows the earliest date, not the expected one
Board ambition of $40M read as a path, since no option the planning team modeled reaches $40M in 2030
The memo's 0.71 correlation between doors and Amazon sales cannot prove Option B's 1.3 times halo; a correlation does not show which one drives the other
The plan's 4.5 units per door comes from the retailer's deck on successful newcomers, which leaves out brands that were removed
Amazon alone does not ensure scale (Gaon Lab, Yeoreum below $5M)
20% awareness is needed, not sufficient, for retail
Management can run one major launch at a time

normalized.extraction_notes: The deck came as plain text, so there were no images to view. Chart values are copied as given; some are decimal shares (e.g. 0.41) and appear here as percentages. Slide 20's timeline is a graphic, so the extracted text does not show which quarter each item falls in. Slide 12's waterfall has a 'base' series, which was left out because it only positions the bars. Slide 24 is a table of actions, so its rows are under next_steps and its claims list is empty. The executive summary lists its sub-bullets after each of the four main points, in order.
